content.text:
Fixed in `lib/request.js:120-144`.

## The bug

`const socketAddr = this.raw.socket?.remoteAddress` yields `undefined` — never `null` — when `raw.socket` is absent, so `socketAddr !== null` was always true in exactly the case it was meant to catch. The guard (added defensively in 8dee9be0 alongside the real #6613 fix) was dead code for a missing socket, and no test exercised its branch.

It was also wrong in the one case where it *did* fire. `proxyAddr.all`, which backs `ip`/`ips`, normalizes a missing/undefined/null `remoteAddress` to `null` and hands that to the trust function, letting it decide. The short-circuit made `host`/`protocol` decide *instead of* `proxyFn`, so the same request disagreed with itself: with `trustProxy: 1` and a null `remoteAddress`, `req.ip` was `1.1.1.1` (from `x-forwarded-for`) while `req.host` ignored `x-forwarded-host`. A literal `null` and an `undefined` `remoteAddress` mean the same thing but took different paths.

## The fix

Normalize with `?? null` and drop the short-circuit, so `host`/`protocol` ask `proxyFn` the identical question `ip`/`ips` ask, with the identical argument. Consequences, verified against `@fastify/proxy-addr`:

- Compiled address lists return `false` for `null`, so untrusted connections still can't spoof forwarded headers — the security test at `test/trust-proxy.test.js:166` passes unchanged.
- Hop-count / `true` / custom functions decide for themselves, keeping the IISNode case (#6606) working.
- Custom trust functions now receive `null` rather than `undefined`, matching proxy-addr's own contract.

## Tests

Added two cases to `test/trust-proxy.test.js` covering the previously untested branches: all three "no address" shapes (missing socket, undefined, null) across both a hop count and an address list, and an assertion that a custom trust fn never sees `undefined`. My first draft of the former asserted `protocol === undefined` for an untrusted socket; that was my error — an existing unencrypted socket correctly falls back to `'http'`, and only a wholly absent socket gives `undefined`. Corrected per case.

`test/trust-proxy.test.js` (12/12), `test/internals/request.test.js`, `test/request-error.test.js`, `test/hostname-port.test.js`, `test/http2/trust-proxy.test.js` (31/31), `test/request-header-host.test.js`, `test/internals/initial-config.test.js` (23/23) all pass. I did not run eslint — the command needed approval. Not committed.

Per the repo's risk map: `buildRegularRequest` needs no mirrored change (its `host`/`protocol` getters never consult `proxyFn`), and the co-change partner `lib/reply.js` has no host/protocol or trust logic, so it needed no change either.
